rationale.conceptual: The method is an established Metropolis Monte Carlo simulation with finite-size scaling analysis. It requires a solid grasp of the model, sublattice decomposition, and scaling relations, but no novel algorithm; it is a non-trivial application of standard statistical physics techniques.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves several sequential stages: Monte Carlo simulations for multiple lattice sizes and anisotropy values, data collection, finite-size scaling fitting to extract η, and pattern density counting. Managing these simulations (thermalization, sweeps, multiple temperatures) and coordinating the analysis constitutes a moderate orchestration complexity.

The method is established but demands careful handling of lattice geometry, observables, and scaling relations; execution involves running many simulations across multiple lattice sizes and parameter values, then analysing the data. The pipeline is moderate but not novel, and the resource needs are purely CPU with low memory.
